scenes.text: This is the review of ws version six, milestone two. A Rust daemon called wsd replaces the zsh version of ws on one machine. The verdict: ready to merge, with one major finding.

What changed: ws runs on one Rust daemon instead of shell scripts and lock files. Commands, flags, output and exit codes stay the same. Look first at change six, messages: delivery moved from the file inbox to log events. The risk is medium, and one command switches back to the zsh backend.
Thirty-five of the thirty-six planned criteria are met. One is partial: the final review is a non-blocking comment, and the human checks are the hand-test list.

Read the fourteen changes in order. One binary holds the CLI, the daemon and the MCP server. Each session has an append-only, hash-chained log, with a SQLite registry as its projection. Sessions get ULIDs and keep their short aliases. In change six, messages become log events with confirmed delivery, as the sequence diagram shows.
The review found one major issue and six minor ones. The major one, an agent launch that can fail under load, is deferred to milestone three. The minor ones are open, and none blocks the merge.
The hand test has eleven steps. Check out the PR head, back up the zsh state, preview the import, then install, which starts the daemon and imports the old state.
To roll back, switch the backend to zsh while the daemon runs, then stop the daemon. To return to Rust, install again and select the Rust backend.
That is milestone two: reviewed, with eleven hand-test steps, and ready to merge. Open the report page for every change, finding and step.
